intro_messages.speaker: Deoran
intro_messages.message: At last we have reunited with the farmers at Southport, Wesnoth’s southernmost bastion of civilization. Ethiliel, will you finally tell us what evil it is we flee from? I have trusted you thus far, but even trust has its limits.

intro_messages.speaker: Ethiliel
intro_messages.message: ...I couldn’t admit it to myself, Deoran. I couldn’t before, and now that he is almost upon us—

intro_messages.speaker: Mebrin
intro_messages.message: Ethiliel... At last, the student reunites with her master. Why do you flee from me?

intro_messages.speaker: Ethiliel
intro_messages.message: Mebrin. I sensed it, but I did not want to believe. ...I could not bear to believe.

intro_messages.speaker: Deoran
intro_messages.message: This is the sage Mebrin? Urza Afalas was right! He has gone mad with power and transformed himself into a lich!

intro_messages.speaker: Mebrin
intro_messages.message: Mad? I am furious!! Those accursed mudlings took me and tormented me, tortured me for sport! I knew that once the first strand of black magic left my hands, there would be no turning back. But I would suffer this humiliation no longer...

intro_messages.speaker: Mebrin
intro_messages.message: I taught the summoning of powers beyond the control of the feeble mudlings, powers that fed upon their race’s filth and greed. Content with only meagre tricks, they never even noticed as I slowly brought them under my thrall! The Urza brothers sought to enslave me, but it is they who became my slaves in the end.

intro_messages.speaker: Mebrin
intro_messages.message: I am called Mal M’Brin now, Ethiliel. It is the name I took when I unchained myself from the shallow-mindedness of the elves and passed over into enlightenment. In a way, I am grateful to these humans. They, though indirectly, have opened my eyes to power I would have never thought possible.

intro_messages.speaker: Deoran
intro_messages.message: Ethiliel, we can’t keep running! I know you don’t want to fight your mentor, but he has been consumed by the dark magic! We have no choice!

intro_messages.speaker: Mebrin
intro_messages.message: No matter. In time she will join me... and in the now, I will finally begin taking my vengeance on humanity, in return for all the suffering your race has inflicted upon me.

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: You see, mortals? This is the might of a true elf; the chosen people of Irdya. The bones of Urza Afalas’s warriors serve only to swell my own ranks.

a.message_mari: That is... a lot of undead. As in, a LOT of undead; way more than we can handle, Deoran. Southport is barely a hamlet — both us and the townsfolk are dead if we fight here.
a.message_gerrick: Sir, look a’ the size o’ that army! Southport is a fine hamlet, but even th’ castle o’ Westin would be ill-equipped for holdin’ back so many. The townsfolk will be slaughtered if we try ’n fight here!
a.message_hylas: Deoran, see the size of that army... I fear this is not a battle we can win. Southport is barely a hamlet — here we have little chance of protecting either our soldiers or the townsfolk.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message_mari: What other option do we have, Captain Mari? “Mal M’Brin” has made it clear he blames all humanity for his suffering. Even if we could escape ourselves, Westin is completely unprepared for an attack!
a.message_gerrick: What other option do we have, Sir Gerrick? “Mal M’Brin” has made it clear he blames all humanity for his suffering. Even if we could escape ourselves, Westin is completely unprepared for an attack!
a.message_hylas: What other option do we have, Minister Hylas? “Mal M’Brin” has made it clear he blames all humanity for his suffering. Even if we could escape ourselves, Westin is completely unprepared for an attack!

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: And besides... the horses are tired, the men are tired and I’m tired as well. The undead can march day and night without rest, but we can’t. Our only choice is to fight, as unlikely as our victory may be.

a.message_mari: Well... that leaves only one option then, doesn’t it? Always thought I had too much good sense for heroics...
Get out of here, Deoran. Leave me the few men you’ve already recruited, but take the others and go warn Westin. I’ll make a stand here. We’ll slow ’em down as much as we can.
a.message_gerrick: Then there’s only one thing we can do. Sir, you must hasten back to Westin t’ warn the garrison. I’ll command the defense here. Leave me th’ few men ye’ve already recruited, and we’ll hold back the undead as long as we can.
a.message_hylas: Then our course of action is clear. Deoran, take the bulk of our company and return to Westin. Warn the garrison and rally a defense. My bad leg would only slow you down — I shall remain behind with the few men you’ve already recruited, and delay the undead as best we can.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: What?! But fighting alone— such a thing will mean certain death! If we stand here together, there is at least a chance we might prevail!

a.message_mari: Yeah yeah, don’t kid yourself. You’ve come a long way since we first met, Deoran, but you’ve still got a lot to learn about war. Westin’s counting on you.
a.message_gerrick: You’re bright, sir, but you’re still young. Ah’ve learned that in dire times, sacrifices must always be made one way or another. Take care o’ yourself, Deoran.
a.message_hylas: How many foes have fallen under your sword, or friends while carrying out your battle-orders? My sacrifice is no more special just because you know my name, Deoran.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message_mari: I... I understand. I will ride with all haste to Westin, to rally the garrison and make ready the defense. Captain Mari, we shall return as soon as we can, and surely relieve you!
a.message_gerrick: I... I understand. I will ride with all haste to Westin, to rally the garrison and make ready the defense. Sir Gerrick, we shall return as soon as we can, and surely relieve you!
a.message_hylas: I... I understand. I will ride with all haste to Westin, to rally the garrison and make ready the defense. Minister Hylas, we shall return as soon as we can, and surely relieve you!

a.message_mari: Sure, relieve us... Look, just don’t do anything stupid without me around to keep an eye on you, okay? Now get out of here before I change my mind.
a.message_gerrick: You know full well what the outcome of our battle here will be. I’m trustin’ you to protect m’ home from the undead; all I ask o’ you is to remember us. Farewell, Sir Deoran!
a.message_hylas: Self-deception does not become you. I only ask that you defeat this lich in the end — do not let our deaths be in vain. May you always serve the light, Deoran.

a.description: Protect Captain Mari as long as possible
Protect Sir Gerrick as long as possible

a.message: I won’t flee like the others, you undead! This is my home and I’ll defend it to the last!

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: Taste cold steel!

a.message_mari: Gold, gold, $gold gold — for the first time in my life I’m rich, except I can’t spend any of it. With the town emptied and our company gone I can’t recruit, so I’ll have to take good care of the few soldiers I have.
a.message_gerrick: $gold gold is more than plenty, but money ain’t much use with th’ town empty and our company gone. I cannae recruit, so I must make the most out o’ every soldier I have.
a.message_hylas: Funds are in no short supply, but $gold gold is of little use with the town emptied and our company departed. I cannot recruit, so I must make each soldier count.

a.message_mari: Is that all you’ve got? After so much bluster, I thought you would have been able to finish me off by now. Guess lichdom isn’t all it’s cracked up to be.
a.message_gerrick: C’mon, is that all you’ve got? I thought liches were supposed to be terrifyin’! I’m not afraid of death, only of failing my people.
a.message_hylas: Lich, you bluster of destructive secrets and powers immemorial. Yet here I stand, and here I yet draw breath. The light shall never surrender to the darkness.

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: The annoyance dares to speak. I will not bandy words with vermin, human.

a.speaker: second_unit
a.message: Take that! Die, invaders!

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: They’ve broken through the trapdoor and entered the refugee cellar! Even if we could still manage to win by force of arms, Westin is doomed without its people...

a.message_mari: Yeah... figures that I wouldn’t get a happy ending. Good luck, rookie...
a.message_gerrick: Urghhh.... Good luck, sir, wherever you are... I only hope we bought enough time...
a.message_hylas: From the light I came... and into the light I go...

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: A pathetic display. Westin will pose no more of a challenge than did this rabble. March onward, my skeletons! We’ll sweep through Westin and raze it to the ground!

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: Pesky humans; you’ve delayed me, but not for long. Westin will pose no more of a challenge than did this rabble. March onward, my skeletons! We’ll sweep through Westin and raze it to the ground!

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: Pesky little humans! You may have delayed me, but my victory is inevitable. March onward, my skeletons! We’ll sweep through Westin and raze it to the ground!

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: Pesky little humans! You may have delayed me for longer than expected, but my victory is inevitable. March onward, my skeletons! We’ll sweep through Westin and raze it to the ground!

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: Infuriating humans! How dare you survive for so long? March onward, my skeletons, we must now make haste! We’ll sweep through Westin and raze it to the ground!

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: What!? Impossible! Beaten by a mere handful of humans? This cannot be! I must purge you all — I must destroy all who live... I must...

a.message_mari: These worthless humans just bested you and your armies. Your time has come, once-wise sage of the elves.
a.message_gerrick: No, I mus’ destroy you. Your time ha’ come, once-wise sage o’ th’ elves.
a.message_hylas: The light will always triumph over the darkness. Your time has come, once-wise sage of the elves.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I have failed my kingdom and duty...

a.speaker: unit
a.message: Yeah... I should’ve figured I wouldn’t get a happy ending...

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I have given all in service of my kingdom...

a.speaker: unit
a.message: May the Light guide you where I have failed...

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I have lost everything helping the humans... Now they will surely perish!

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I perish! Such wasted potential! I’d gained much experience, and was close to becoming something more...

a.speaker: narrator
a.message: One of your high-experience units has died! Take care to protect your experienced soldiers, so that they can eventually advance to powerful Level 2 veterans.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: Argh, I fall! All my hard-won battle experience is lost! I will not be easy to replace, Deoran...

a.speaker: narrator
a.message: One of your high-level veterans has died! Take care to protect your promoted soldiers, so that you can recall them in future battles.

a.speaker: narrator
a.message: One of your units has reached max XP, and has advanced a level! It is now significantly more powerful, and has been fully healed! For a full description of what one of your units can do, right-click it and select “Unit Type Description.”
My healing magic is potent, but I cannot use it to heal myself. I’ll have to spend some time in a village to recover.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I missed all $consecutive_misses strikes! I tried my best, but this enemy had a high chance to evade. I might have had better odds attacking a different enemy.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: A good commander understands the odds, and knows how to both exploit good luck and mitigate bad luck. After all, both good and bad luck are equally likely!

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I got lucky and hit all $consecutive_hits strikes! Good luck will sometimes happen, but a good commander knows how to win without relying on it. After all, bad luck happens just as often as good luck!

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I missed all $consecutive_misses strikes, even though my enemy had a low chance to evade! That’s unlucky, but bad luck happens just as often as good luck — a good commander knows how to plan around both!

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I hit all $consecutive_hits strikes, even though my enemy had a high chance to evade! Luck works both ways — sometimes I miss strikes when I was likely to hit, but sometimes I also hit strikes that I was likely to miss — like now!

a.speaker: unit
a.message: Our bows and spears are nearly useless against these skeletons! They have nothing for our shafts to pierce but air!
